name: Cursor
description: AI-first code editor with whole-project awareness, tab completion and a multi-file agent.
free_limit: Hobby plan: limited agent requests + 2,000 tab completions/month
notes: Free tier is an evaluation budget, not a workflow. Pair it with Gemini CLI or Cline for the heavy lifting.

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
description: Agentic editor from Cognition — the Windsurf/Cascade lineage, renamed after the 2026 acquisition.
free_limit: Free plan: unlimited tab completion, quota-limited Cascade agent sessions
notes: windsurf.com now redirects to devin.ai. Tab completion is unlimited on every plan, including free — the agent quota is what runs out.

name: GitHub Copilot Free
description: Copilot's genuinely free tier inside VS Code, JetBrains and the GitHub web editor.
free_limit: 2,000 completions + 50 chat/agent requests per month
notes: Requires any GitHub account, including free. Best free choice if you already live in VS Code.

name: Zed
description: Rust-native, GPU-accelerated editor with a free built-in AI tier and bring-your-own-key support.
free_limit: Free AI tier included; unlimited use with your own API keys

name: Kiro
description: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE — writes requirements and design docs before it writes code.
free_limit: Free tier with monthly agentic-interaction quota

name: Trae
description: ByteDance's AI IDE with a free tier built around frontier models and an agent mode.
free_limit: Free plan with monthly premium-model requests
notes: Review the data-retention policy before using it on proprietary code.

name: Amp (Sourcegraph)
description: Frontier agent from Sourcegraph with a free-forever plan, then pay-as-you-go with no subscription required.
free_limit: Free plan with a monthly ad-supported allowance; BYOK option

name: OpenCode
description: Open-source terminal coding agent with a client/server architecture and provider-agnostic model routing.
free_limit: Free software — you bring a model key (free tiers work fine)

name: Kilo Code
description: Open-source VS Code agent with a large free model allocation before you need your own key.
free_limit: Free credits on signup for Anthropic/Gemini models; unlimited with BYOK

name: Gemini CLI
description: Google's open-source terminal agent with the most generous free quota of any first-party CLI.
free_limit: 1,000 requests/day with a personal Google account (60 RPM)
notes: Also ships a free Gemini Code Assist VS Code extension on the same account. The best $0 coding agent in 2026.

name: Qwen Code
description: Qwen's fork of Gemini CLI wired to Qwen3-Coder, with a large free daily request allowance via OAuth.
free_limit: ~2,000 requests/day via Qwen OAuth
notes: Strong on large refactors thanks to Qwen3-Coder's context window. The 2,000/day figure is subject to change.

name: Aider
description: Terminal pair-programmer that commits every change to git and maps your repo into the model's context.
free_limit: Free software — works with any free LLM API key

name: Cline
description: Autonomous coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal, with human approval at every step.
free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key (including free tiers)
notes: The most flexible free setup: point it at Gemini or Groq free tiers and a full agent costs nothing.

name: Roo Code
description: Cline fork with custom modes (architect, debugger, tester) and an orchestrator mode for multi-step work.
free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

name: Continue
description: Open-source Copilot alternative for VS Code and JetBrains with customisable model routing.
free_limit: Free software; connect Ollama for genuinely unlimited local use

name: OpenHands
description: Open-source software engineering agent (formerly OpenDevin) that runs in a sandboxed container.
free_limit: Free software; hosted version has limited free credits

name: Goose
description: Block's local-first agent that can extend itself by writing its own MCP extensions.
free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

name: Crush
description: Charm's glamorous terminal agent with MCP support, LSP awareness and session management.
free_limit: Free and open source — bring any provider key

name: LangGraph
description: Stateful, graph-based agent orchestration with durable execution, human-in-the-loop and time travel.
free_limit: Open source (MIT). LangGraph Platform has a free developer tier
notes: Choose this over raw LangChain when your agent needs to pause, resume or survive a crash mid-run.

name: LangChain
description: The widest integration ecosystem in the space — 600+ tools, loaders and vector store connectors.
free_limit: Open source (MIT); no account required

name: LlamaIndex
description: Data framework for RAG: ingestion, chunking, indexing and query engines over your own documents.
free_limit: Open source (MIT); LlamaCloud has a limited free tier

name: CrewAI
description: Role-based multi-agent crews with delegation, sequential and hierarchical process modes.
free_limit: Open source (MIT)

name: AG2 (AutoGen)
description: Microsoft-originated multi-agent conversation framework: agents that talk to each other until the task is done.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
description: Small, provider-agnostic agent SDK: handoffs, guardrails, sessions and tracing in a few hundred lines.
free_limit: Open source (MIT); works with any provider, not just OpenAI
notes: Despite the name, it is vendor-neutral — point it at Gemini or Groq and it works unchanged.

name: Google Agent Development Kit
description: Google's agent framework with a built-in dev UI, evaluation harness and A2A protocol support.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: Pydantic AI
description: Type-safe agent framework from the Pydantic team — validated structured outputs and dependency injection.
free_limit: Open source (MIT)

name: smolagents
description: Hugging Face's minimal agent library — code-writing agents in under 1,000 lines of core logic.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: Agno
description: High-performance multi-modal agent framework with built-in memory, knowledge and reasoning tools.
free_limit: Open source (MPL 2.0)

name: DSPy
description: Programs language models instead of prompting them — optimisers compile prompts against a metric.
free_limit: Open source (MIT)

name: Haystack
description: Production RAG and agent pipelines from deepset, with strong evaluation and deployment tooling.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: Letta
description: Stateful agents with long-term memory that manage their own context window (formerly MemGPT).
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0); free cloud sandbox available

name: Semantic Kernel
description: Microsoft's enterprise agent SDK for Python, .NET and Java with planners and process framework.
free_limit: Open source (MIT)

name: Mastra
description: TypeScript agent framework with workflows, evals, RAG and local dev playground.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: Vercel AI SDK
description: The standard TypeScript toolkit for streaming UI plus agents, with unified provider interfaces.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: LiteLLM
description: One OpenAI-shaped interface over 100+ providers, with a proxy that adds budgets, keys and tracing.
free_limit: Open source (MIT)
notes: The cleanest way to stack several free tiers behind one endpoint and fail over automatically when one 429s.

name: n8n
description: Node-based automation with native AI agent nodes, MCP trigger and hundreds of integrations.
free_limit: Self-hosted Community Edition is free forever (fair-code licence)
notes: Running the Docker image on a free-tier VM is the cheapest credible production agent host in this list.

name: Dify
description: LLMOps platform for building chat agents, workflows and RAG apps with a visual editor and API output.
free_limit: Self-hosted Community Edition free; cloud sandbox free tier

name: Langflow
description: Visual drag-and-drop builder that compiles to LangChain-based flows and exposes each as an API.
free_limit: Open source (MIT)

name: Flowise
description: Low-code LLM orchestration with agent flows, tools and embeddable chat widgets.
free_limit: Open source (Apache 2.0)

name: Activepieces
description: Open-source Zapier alternative with AI pieces and MCP support, MIT-licensed rather than fair-code.
free_limit: Self-hosted Community Edition free (MIT)

name: MemPalace
description: Local-first memory for agents that stores conversations verbatim in ChromaDB and organises them into wings, halls and rooms instead of letting an LLM decide what is worth keeping.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, runs locally with zero API calls
notes: Co-created by Milla Jovovich and Ben Sigman.

Often quoted as "100% on benchmarks" — that is the hybrid pipeline with cloud reranking, which the authors themselves flagged as tuned on failing questions. The defensible numbers are 96.6% R@5 raw on LongMemEval with zero API calls and a 98.4% held-out hybrid score.
The project publicly walked back an overstated "30x lossless compression" claim; its experimental AAAK mode actually regresses to 84.2%.

name: Cognee
description: Open-source memory platform that builds a self-hosted knowledge graph from your data, giving agents persistent long-term memory across sessions.
free_limit: Free — self-hosted, runs with local extraction and embedding models
notes: Runs end to end without an OpenAI or Anthropic key by using local extraction and embedding models, which is unusual for knowledge-graph memory. A hosted tier exists for teams that would rather not self-host.

name: Mem0
description: Drop-in memory layer for agents that extracts and stores salient facts between sessions, with the widest framework support of any memory library.
free_limit: Free open-source self-host; hosted tier includes 10K memories
notes: The most-starred memory project by a wide margin. Extraction-based like its benchmarks measure against — it summarises rather than storing verbatim, so recall depends on the extraction step. The hosted platform is a paid product beyond the free allowance.

name: Nanobrowser
description: Open-source Chrome extension that runs multi-agent web workflows — extract, compare and fill forms — inside your own browser, on your own keys.
free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0 extension, works with any provider including Ollama and Groq
notes: The pitch is "open-source alternative to OpenAI Operator", and its real advantage is BYOK: pair it with Ollama for a fully local browser agent, or with a free Groq/Gemini key. Chrome-family browsers only.

name: Freebuff
description: Coding agent funded by terminal advertising — desktop, CLI, web and chat clients all backed by frontier models at no cost, in exchange for text ads.
free_limit: Free with ad support; no subscription
notes: Marked degraded rather than active because the business model is the product: the vendor sells terminal ad impressions to fund inference, so model access and the ad load can both change without notice. Closed source, and the "unlimited" wording is marketing — throughput is throttled in practice. Do not point anything production-critical at it.

name: KISS Sorcar
description: Local-first agent framework that runs as a VS Code extension plus web and mobile clients, routing to any of hundreds of models across nine provider categories.
free_limit: Free framework (Apache-2.0) — pay only your model provider
notes: The "KISS" in the name is the design brief. Provider counts and third-party agent integrations move quickly in this project, so treat any specific number (661 models, 43 agents) as a snapshot rather than a spec.

name: ReadyAgents Core
description: Self-hosted workflow engine and MCP toolkit that records agent runs so you can replay them offline, fork a run, diff two runs, or freeze one into a regression test.
free_limit: Free — self-hosted, bring your own provider keys
notes: The record/replay/diff loop is the genuinely unusual part — most agent frameworks still have no first-class way to turn a production run into a regression test.

name: NanoBot
description: Deliberately tiny personal-agent framework from the HKU Data Intelligence lab that reimplements most of a large agent stack in roughly 4K lines.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, bring your own provider keys
notes: Actively developed by a research lab and worth reading end-to-end precisely because it is small. The "90% of OpenClaw's capabilities" figure is the project's own framing, not a measured comparison.

name: Pincer
description: Self-hosted personal agent that lives in your messaging apps — WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Signal and email — with a large native tool set plus everything reachable over MCP.
free_limit: Free — self-hosted via Docker, bring your own keys
notes: Skill signing and audit logs are the differentiators: an agent wired into your WhatsApp can take real actions on your behalf, so its security posture matters more than a coding agent's.

name: QwenPaw
description: Personal assistant agent that runs fully locally against its own bundled QwenPaw-Flash models, so it needs no API key and no cloud account at all.
free_limit: Free — local models included (2B/4B/9B)
notes: Genuinely key-free out of the box rather than BYOK, which is rare. Connectors skew to Chinese platforms (DingTalk, Lark, WeChat, QQ) alongside Discord, Telegram and iMessage. A 2B-9B local model is a capable assistant, not a frontier-reasoning substitute.

name: Tares
description: Self-hostable data plane for always-on agents: ingest events from Prometheus, OpenTelemetry and webhooks, then let an MCP server act on them.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, runs on your own machine
notes: Targets the gap between "an agent that answers" and one that reacts to what your infrastructure is actually doing.

name: Kitaru
description: Durable-execution runtime for Python agents from the ZenML team: record, replay and improve agent runs in production.
free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, self-hosted
notes: Submitted as "ZenML/Kitaru"; the canonical repository is zenml-io/kitaru. Built by the team behind ZenML, which is the main reason to trust it at this age.

name: Nexora
description: Self-hosted orchestration platform where agents get personas, skills and tools, with sub-agent delegation, RAG and semantic memory.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed self-hosted core
notes: Early-stage (tens of stars, commits this month). Useful if you want a self-hosted multi-agent UI today; audit it before pointing it at anything sensitive.

name: Automatos AI
description: Apache-2.0 multi-agent orchestration platform built around RAG and vector embeddings, able to route through free provider tiers including NVIDIA's.
free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, bring your own keys
notes: Judge it as a multi-agent orchestration stack; the "neural field theory" framing is not an evaluable claim.

name: aigate
description: Single-compose self-hosted AI platform bundling inference, tool use, browser automation, image generation, speech synthesis, transcription and object storage.
free_limit: Free — self-hosted; bundled providers have their own free tiers
notes: Small project with a wide attack surface — one compose file exposing inference, storage and code execution. Read the compose file before exposing it beyond localhost.

name: miii-cli
description: Offline coding agent for the terminal that runs entirely on Ollama, positioned as a local alternative to Claude Code, Cursor and Copilot.
free_limit: Free forever — MIT licensed, no keys, no cloud
notes: Small but actively developed. Output quality tracks whichever local model you point it at, so pair it with a decent coding model rather than a 3B.

name: PawWork
description: Desktop agent for macOS and Windows with free models bundled in, aimed at office files, web search and scheduled automations rather than code.
free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, bundled models need no API key
notes: The no-key, no-terminal framing makes it a genuine on-ramp for non-developers. Bundled free models change without notice, since they depend on upstream providers.

name: Code Buddy
description: Local-first coding agent that reads your repo, writes code and runs commands, with terminal, HTTP and optional desktop interfaces plus fleet collaboration.
free_limit: Free — runs at $0 with Ollama; optional ChatGPT subscription integration
notes: The Ollama path is the supported free route and is why this is listed. Its optional ChatGPT-subscription mode routes through a consumer account rather than an API, which is outside that provider's terms — use the local path.

name: BrowserOS
description: Open-source agentic browser — a Chromium-based alternative to ChatGPT Atlas, Perplexity Comet and Dia, with agents built into the browser rather than bolted on.
free_limit: Free — AGPL-3.0, bring your own model keys
notes: The submission pointed at a one-star fork (gHashTag/BrowserOS); this is the upstream project. AGPL-3.0 matters if you plan to redistribute a modified build.

name: UI-TARS Desktop
description: ByteDance's multimodal GUI agent stack that drives a real desktop — clicking, typing and navigating native apps — from screenshots and instructions.
free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0, run the model locally or bring a key
notes: One of the few computer-use stacks with real industrial backing and a permissive licence. A GUI agent that can click anything on your screen is a large security decision — run it in a VM or on a spare machine.

name: Open Cowork
description: Desktop agent for Windows and macOS that installs Claude Code and MCP tooling in one click and runs the agent in a sandbox.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, bring your own keys
notes: Sandbox isolation is the feature that matters here — the whole point of this class of tool is letting an agent act on your machine, and the sandbox is what bounds the blast radius.

name: Abu-Cowork
description: Local-first desktop agent with self-evolving skills and multi-model support, built as a privacy-preserving alternative to hosted coworking agents.
free_limit: Free — open source, bring your own keys
notes: Mid-sized community project. "Self-evolving skills" means it writes new skills for itself over time — keep an eye on what it accumulates.

name: HyperDesk
description: Desktop coding workbench where the agent reads the project, runs commands, drives a browser and coordinates subagents — asking before it changes anything.
free_limit: Free — open source, bring your own keys
notes: The confirm-before-changing behaviour is the right default for a tool with this much reach. Young project — check the package's own release notes before trusting it with a large repo.

name: Alice Memory
description: Local-first continuity layer that lets agents resume interrupted work, track open loops and recall decisions with provenance, exposed over MCP, HTTP and CLI.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, local, no API keys
notes: Provenance — remembering why a decision was made, not just what it was — is the part most memory layers skip. The 79.4% LongMemEval figure is the project's own reported number, not independently reproduced here.

name: Mazu
description: Coding-agent CLI with a memory and checkpoint layer: it keeps a queryable record of project decisions, conventions and past mistakes across sessions.
free_limit: Free — open source, bring your own keys
notes: Pair it with any of the free coding models catalogued here. As with every local memory store, the retrieval quality matters more than the storage format.

name: pi-coding-agent
description: Minimal, inspectable coding agent that persists project facts to a plain .pi/memory.md file instead of a hidden database, with self-review and autonomous tool use.
free_limit: Free — open source, multi-provider
notes: Storing memory as readable Markdown you can edit and review is the whole appeal — no opaque vector store to debug when recall goes wrong.

name: mengram-ai
description: Human-like memory layer for agents with auto-save, auto-recall and a cognitive profile, split across semantic, episodic and procedural memory and exposed as MCP tools.
free_limit: Free — open source, runs locally
notes: Splitting memory into semantic, episodic and procedural stores is a more honest model of how agents actually benefit from memory than a single flat vector index. Actively released and includes Claude Code hooks.

name: haiku.rag
description: Agentic RAG that runs locally by default, using Ollama-hosted open models for the full pipeline — ingestion, embeddings, retrieval and generation.
free_limit: Free — open source; the default pipeline needs no external API key
notes: Scales from a laptop to a server without changing the stack, and the no-key default is the reason it belongs in this catalogue rather than in a generic RAG list.

name: Pinakes
description: Portable, agent-first knowledge base where one directory holds the corpus, retrieved with SQLite FTS5 lexical search plus local embeddings and local reranking.
free_limit: Free — no API key needed to search or re-index
notes: Combining BM25 with embeddings is more robust than either alone — lexical search catches exact identifiers that pure vector search misses, and re-indexing costs nothing.

name: Arc Rector
description: Agentic RAG stack assembled entirely from open-source components, with nine swappable layers so you can replace any piece without touching the rest.
free_limit: Free — open source, no API keys, no vendor bills
notes: Worth reading as a reference architecture even if you do not adopt it — the swappable-layer structure is a clean answer to RAG stacks that hard-code one vendor.

name: local-rag-assistant
description: Chat with any codebase locally: AST-aware chunking, Ollama embeddings and a Chroma vector store, with no code leaving your machine.
free_limit: Free — fully local, no API keys
notes: AST-aware chunking beats naive line splitting on code, because a function is the unit you actually want retrieved. Small community project — read before you run.

name: Pleias SLM RAG
description: On-device RAG API built on a ~300M-parameter model small enough to run on a Raspberry Pi 5, with no GPU and no external API calls.
free_limit: Free — Apache-2.0 model weights
notes: Genuinely edge-sized, which is rare for anything labelled RAG. A 300M model is for retrieval and grounded short answers, not general reasoning.

name: HOL Guard
description: Antivirus and runtime protection layer for agent tooling — plugins, skills and MCP servers — that sits between your agent and the code it is about to run.
free_limit: Free — runs locally, no account
notes: Installing an MCP server means running someone else's code with your credentials in reach; this is one of the few tools treating that as the security boundary it is. Integrates with the major agent CLIs.

name: agent-bom
description: Scanner and self-hosted control plane for AI infrastructure — sweeps agent configs, MCP servers, instruction files, containers, cloud estate and model artefacts.
free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted
notes: The agent-specific targets — instruction files and MCP configs — are what distinguish it from a generic container scanner. Actively released.

name: PanGuard
description: One-command monitoring and guarding for agents and MCP servers, aimed at catching what an agent does rather than what it was asked to do.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed, 100% open source
notes: Deliberately low-friction — one command and it starts watching, which is the right trade for teams that will not stand up a full security stack.

name: Bawbel Scanner
description: Security scanner for MCP servers and AI skill files that scores findings against OWASP's AIVSS rubric and ships an open vulnerability database with a public API.
free_limit: Free — open source
notes: Scoring MCP servers against a published rubric is useful because it makes two servers comparable. AIVSS is still evolving, so treat scores as guidance rather than verdicts.

name: Nightona
description: Community continuation of Daytona: elastic sandbox infrastructure for running AI-generated code and agent workflows in isolation.
free_limit: Free — AGPL-3.0, self-hosted
notes: Forked from Daytona's last AGPL-3.0 release after that project changed direction, so the licence is what makes the continuation legitimate — and it means you inherit the maintenance burden rather than a vendor's.

name: Capka
description: Self-hosted sandbox for AI agents, built as a community alternative to hosted coworking sandboxes.
free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted
notes: Young project — verify the isolation boundary yourself before trusting it with untrusted code, since that is precisely the promise being made.

name: coder-eval
description: Agent-agnostic framework for evaluating and benchmarking coding agents and skills, with support for comparing different agent harnesses head to head.
free_limit: Free — open source
notes: Agent-agnostic is the valuable property: you can A/B your own agent against a reference harness instead of trusting a vendor's self-reported score.

name: OpenMCP
description: Self-hosted benchmarking harness for computer-use agents acting through MCP, letting you measure tool-using agents reproducibly.
free_limit: Free — open source, self-hosted
notes: Computer-use evaluation is the least standardised corner of agent testing, so any harness that makes results reproducible is worth knowing about. Early-stage project.

name: agent-eval
description: Evaluation framework that auto-generates test tasks for an agent, executes them and scores results across several dimensions.
free_limit: Free — open source
notes: Auto-generated tasks solve the blank-page problem in agent testing, but they measure what the generator thought to ask — combine with your own regression cases.

name: BenchClaw
description: Multi-dimensional agent evaluation that scores runs across ten dimensions and visualises the spread as radar charts.
free_limit: Free — MIT licensed
notes: Multi-dimensional scoring is more informative than a single pass/fail number. The advertised "17-judge AI tribunal" and deception detection are separate LLM calls judging output — treat their verdicts as signal, not ground truth.
